newsitem.title: USA: Dayton 4-wk Dec same-store sales up 4.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dayton 4-wk Dec same-store sales up 4.2 pct.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said same-store sales for the four weeks ended December 28 were up 4.2 percent compared with the period ended December 30, 1995.

"Results at Target and Mervyn's for the four weeks were on plan, while department stores sales were below our expectations," said Dayton chief executive Bob Ulrich. "With the shorter selling season this year, we planned our sales conservatively and generally met our plans for the season."

For the year-over-year comparison, the 1995 sales base was shifted one week from Dayton Hudson's fiscal calendar, it said. Four-week December comparable-store sales on this basis by operating division were as follows:
-- Target's comparable-store sales for the four weeks increased 7.1 percent.
-- Mervyn's comparable-store sales for the four weeks decreased 4.1 percent.
-- The Department Store division's comparable-store sales for the four weeks increased 0.3 percent, Dayton said.
Dayton said it will release sales results for the customary fiscal month of December (five weeks of results) on January 9.

The company said its "expectations for the five-week period now include generally flat comparable-store sales at Target, and a high-single to low-double-digit comparable-store sales decline at Mervyn's and the department store division."
Dayton's 1,101 discount and department stores are located in 38 states. They include 736 Target stores, 300 Mervyn's stores and 65 department stores.
